findings.body:
The epic's definition of done states its five [A<n>] marks on one line, and internal/acceptance's parser takes a bracketed [A<n>] only at a line's start (a mid-line bracket is a reference, never a definition), so the record carries exactly one item of record — A1 — and [A2]..[A5] are references nothing can key on: no command can bind evidence to them and a finding cannot name the item it breaks. This epic paid for it twice — its round-1 review's blocking finding (the committed screenshots, [A3]/[A5] material) carried no breaks claim, so the run's absorption had to fall back on the reviewer basis rather than a done-item claim — and it is the same defect the ymf review filed low, recurring one day after ymf's own record was re-flowed. Tick 1ip, open, records it. The tracker edit this finding carries re-marks the same five items one per line — the same words, nothing dropped — so the machinery the epic's close-out feeds (the epic PR's done-evidence section, the [evidence.acceptance] table, a future finding's breaks claim) can address all five.
evidence: .tick/issues/ozw.json acceptance_criteria (one line, [A1]..[A5]); internal/acceptance/acceptance.go:18 (attemptedMark is line-anchored)
tracker edit: acceptance_criteria of ozw (applied by the run)
findings.title: Re-flow ozw's acceptance criteria so [A1]..[A5] parse as five items

findings.body:
The one-item-per-line rule was written into the learnings at ymf's close-out and applied to ymf's own record the same day; ozw was planned one line again the next morning, spent the whole epic with [A2]..[A5] unkeyable, and its round-1 review could not name the item its blocking finding broke. The run's only reader of an epic's criteria is the PR's done-evidence section, after the fact (internal/reconcile/pr_reviewer.go:220); nothing checks the record when the epic is claimed or admitted, so the rule rests on the planner reading a learnings file at the moment of writing the record. The check is cheap — acceptance.Parse against the [A<n>] marks the text carries — and the repair channel already exists (the tracker edit): a run that admits an epic whose marks parse as fewer items than it marks should re-flow it or refuse, not blind its own evidence binding for the epic's whole life and repair the record at close-out.
evidence: .tick/issues/ozw.json acceptance_criteria (one line, [A1]..[A5]) against .tick/issues/ymf.json (re-flowed 2026-10-09, the day before ozw was created); internal/reconcile/pr_reviewer.go:220 (the only acceptance.Parse reader, post hoc)
findings.title: A run admits an epic whose acceptance marks parse as fewer items than it marks

findings.body:
The ozw close-out's retro, as the whole new .tick/learnings.md. It is a compaction, not an append: the file is at its 150-line hard cap, so two rules gain the halves this epic paid for — the prose-data rule gains the enforcement point (ozw's five marks went one line again the day after ymf's re-flow, and its round-1 review could key no item onto its blocking finding: the rule is enforced where the record is first read, not repaired at close-out), and the gate-coverage rule gains committed rendered evidence as the same claim (ozw's five watch PNGs aged under three green merges — the gate pins the frames they render, nothing tied the images to them — so an epic that names committed screenshots puts the re-capture in the tick that LAST changes a pinned frame, or asserts the capture sources in the gate) — and two same-family merges come out (the two boundary pairs into one; the dz1 resume pair into the hn6 restart pair it shares a family with), at exactly 150 lines. A cloud close-out still cannot commit the file itself (tick 3hw, open: the container's pre-commit hook refuses every .tick/ path), so it rides this protected change as bo9's and ymf's did.
protected change: a new .tick/learnings.md (applied by the run after its close-out, for the merger to review)
findings.title: Apply the ozw close-out retro: the compacted .tick/learnings.md
